source.title: Measuring Affinity between Attention-Head Weight Subspaces via the Projection Kernel
source.authors: Hiroaki Yamagiwa; Yusuke Takase; H. Shimodaira

record.tranche_reason: The study compares weight-similarity metrics by how well they recover IOI-annotated head classes in GPT2-small, bearing on whether different metrics recover the same circuit. It does not intervene on the circuit or test IOI behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper uses IOI head annotations as labels and evaluates head-pair similarity metrics against them. It also reports evaluations in other models, but these measure recovery of annotations, not whether those models perform IOI through the claimed circuit. No IOI behavior, ablation, patching, or faithfulness/completeness/minimality results are reported.
record.test_reason: The study uses IOI head-class annotations from Wang et al. (2023), which it modifies, as ground-truth labels. It then scores how well its own weight-subspace metric (PK) and four baselines recover those labels. It runs no IOI behaviour test, no ablation or patching, and no faithfulness, completeness or minimality check. It does not ask whether the circuit holds or whether another circuit-finding method recovers the same circuit. The PR-AUC tables (Tables 1, 2, 4, 5) report the proposed metric's performance against baselines with the annotations treated as fixed truth, so they say nothing about whether any version of the claim holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that PK captures known IOI head relationships more clearly than CS and other baselines, though its OV performance trails Linear CKA and Procrustes Similarity. They also identify L4H7 as an Identity Head acting as a hub. They note the evaluation relies on IOI annotations, which they modified: they replaced L0H10 with L0H5 and added Previous Token and Induction heads by their own head scores. They also note that some relationships reported by Wang et al. do not appear under PK. They make no claim about the causal IOI circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures global weight-subspace overlap and compares similarity metrics against annotated head classes; it does not perform the original study's prompt-dependent causal circuit interventions, head ablations, or activation patching.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by weight pairing and metric: PK leads on OQ/OK detection but not OV; same-type classification performance also varies by metric and class.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-independent weight-subspace overlap (PK) in GPT2-small reproduces some IOI head relationships: OQ edges from S-Inhibition L8H10 to Name Mover L9H6 and Backup Name Movers L10H1/L10H6. It misses others even with the top 30 edges: Duplicate Token and Induction outputs to S-Inhibition keys have small PK. Section 6.2.2 and Limitations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The IOI head-to-head interactions found by causal analysis are partly visible in static weight geometry, without running inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Heads in the same IOI class show higher same-type weight-subspace overlap than chance, though classwise PR-AUC is very low in an imbalanced setting (mean 0.047). PK leads for most classes; CS beats PK for Previous Token Heads and Procrustes Similarity for Name Mover Heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI head classes correspond to shared weight subspaces.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No causal interventions or behavioral IOI evaluation; the study evaluates recovery of labels inherited from prior head annotations. The reported AUCs do not establish causal roles, circuit faithfulness, completeness, or minimality.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant GPT2-small head-detection or classwise summary results from Tables 1 and 2 were left out. Evaluations on BLOOM-560M and Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct are not included as claim-version rows because they assess annotation recovery rather than whether those models use the claimed IOI mechanism.

untested.parts: The 26-head circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not tested; the annotations are used as labels.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no measure of self-repair.
BLOOM-560M and Qwen2-0.5B use head classes from Zhang et al. (2025) as labels. Whether those models carry IOI through the same circuit is not tested.
No causal circuit-finding method, ablation type or IOI metric is compared. Weight-similarity metrics are benchmarked against the labels instead.
No ablation, metric or prompt distribution is varied for circuit faithfulness or completeness.
No IOI prompt variants are tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 link conflates 'similarity metrics agree with labels' with 'circuit-finding methods recover the same circuit.' This is a metric benchmark using the circuit as ground truth, so it is T4. The annotation set (36 heads) differs from the original 26-head circuit.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head circuit, its causal roles, and the authors' faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not tested.
No main name-mover heads are ablated and no self-repair is measured.

The paper evaluates detection of IOI-annotated heads in BLOOM-560M and Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct, but does not test whether those models carry IOI through the same functional circuit or reuse its components for other tasks.
The study compares weight-similarity metrics against IOI head annotations; it does not compare ablation types or causal circuit-finding procedures.
No IOI performance evaluation or ablation-based faithfulness/completeness measure is varied by metric, intervention, or prompt distribution.
No IOI prompt variants, name orders, templates, or numbers of names are behaviorally tested.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compare top-edge wiring diagrams from PK and CS against IOI head-class annotations
rows.measure: Presence of annotated head-to-head relationships in wiring diagrams
rows.value: The paper reports that the S-Inhibition-to-Name-Mover-related OQ edges visible under PK are absent under CS, including in the top-30 CS diagram.
rows.note: The authors also report that CS captures fewer Previous-Token-to-Induction relationships and that its wiring diagram differs from PK.
rows.check: Compares the wiring diagrams of two weight metrics (PK vs CS). That CS misses the L8H10 OQ edges shows CS is a weaker metric. It does not show that a circuit-finding method recovers a different IOI circuit.

relation.reason: IOI head classes supply evaluation labels; the reported similarity benchmarks do not test IOI behavior, causal circuit sufficiency, backup compensation, or circuit recovery under alternative interventions.

tranche.reason: The study uses existing IOI head annotations, with modifications, to benchmark similarity metrics. These results measure annotation recovery rather than whether any claim version holds.

source_check.notes: All sampled values match Tables 1–2. Appendix H.2 modifies the original annotations, including replacing L0H10 with L0H5 and revising Previous Token and Induction membership; the resulting 36 annotated heads are a method benchmark, not validation of the original 26-head circuit.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small, OQ/OK/OV head detection and same-type head-class classification
reader_labels.reason: Metric recovery varies by pairing: PK leads OQ and OK detection but trails Linear CKA and Procrustes Similarity on OV; classwise results also differ by metric. See R1-R25.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The paper says IOI-related OQ links from S-Inhibition to Name-Mover-related heads appear under PK but are absent under CS, so the compared metrics do not recover identical relationships. See R26.
